Daniel / Mike —

Following up with the sizing pass (assumptions and recommendations). I’m pasting the short rationale and the numbers so procurement can see the tradeoffs quickly.

Assumptions
- Workload mix: 70% chat (instruct-style generation), 30% short classification/rerank.
- Model families: for planning we used an open 13B instruction model for chat and a 7B retriever/classifier for short calls. Both quantized to 4/8-bit execution profiles.
- Avg generation length: 130 tokens; average request includes 1,200 tokens of context. KV caching expected to save ~45% of attention compute on repeat patient lookups.
- Batch window: 10–15ms; continuous batching enabled in runtime.
- Target latency for committed pool: p50 ~150–220ms, p95 <350ms for chat under normal peak; p99 may exceed during sustained extreme surges.

Sizing scenarios (H100-equivalent units)
1) Efficient baseline (recommended starter commit)
- Initial reserved pool: 3 x H100-equivalent GPUs
- Autoscale buffer: burst to 5 GPUs for sustained peak windows (on-demand burst policy)
- Expected steady throughput: ~600–900 chat requests/sec aggregate when batching and KV cache applied (note: this is multi-model mix; effective concurrent sessions supported ~150–220 depending on user behavior)
- Suitable if Orchid accepts short peak queues (~100–120ms extra p95 during >20 minute surges)

2) Conservative production commit (12-month recommended)
- Reserved pool: 5 x H100-equivalent GPUs (steady)
- Autoscale buffer: burst to 8 GPUs for peaks (policy-based, billed by burst minutes)
- Expected steady throughput: ~1,000–1,600 chat requests/sec aggregate with SLA headroom (p95 <350ms under sustained peak). This covers 280 concurrent observed peaks with margin.

Notes on context length and caching
- Long contexts increase per-request memory pressure; the models above assume 80GB-class memory (H100 80GB). If contexts trend above 3k tokens regularly, we recommend moving to 2x memory-per-GPU (or use model sharding) which effectively increases GPU-equivalent count.
- KV cache: for chat flows with repeating patient metadata, effective compute reduction is significant. If your usage pattern has low repetition, plan for the conservative sizing.

Recommended next step
- Anchor approach: start with the Efficient baseline (3-reserved + burst) for 3 months at a reduced committed rate so Orchid can validate traffic. If 95th/99th usage validates, we flip to the 12-month conservative commit (5 reserved) with a retroactive credit structure.

I’ll attach the quick throughput calculators and a one-page runbook. Ben — can you add the pricing scenarios?

— Marissa
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Quick pricing scenarios (high level). All numbers are presented as illustrative line items we will convert into a formal quote PDF and DocuSign. Prices assume US region and H100-equivalent performance. Taxes, KMS/HSM integrations, and professional services are additional line items.

Option A — Anchor trial (3-reserved)

- Anchor period: 3 months
- Committed rate: $19,500 / GPU / month (billed monthly) → $58,500 / month pre-tax
- Autoscale burst: $0.35 / GPU-minute (billed for minutes above reserved pool)
- Retroactive conversion credit: If Orchid converts to the 12-month commit within 90 days of anchor end, we credit 50% of anchor payments toward the committed minimum (to reduce friction).

Option B — 12-month conservative commit (5-reserved)
- Committed reserved: 5 H100-equivalent GPUs
- Base committed rate: $17,500 / GPU / month (net) → $87,500 / month pre-tax
- Discount tiers (applied to base committed rate): 12-month = 18% off list, 24-month = 28% off list. Example: 12-month net after standard discount above reflected in the base committed rate.
- Burst policy: autoscale to 8 GPUs for peaks at $0.28 / GPU-minute (capped monthly).
- SLO: p95 <350ms for chat under committed pool (applies when traffic routed to reserved pool and not under a declared regional outage). We include creditable SLAs by request in the contract (specific credit framework will be in the quote).

Other notes
- Minimum notice for changes to reserved count during anchor: 30 days. For committed 12-month: reserved count changes allowed at month boundaries with 60-day notice and prorated adjustments.
- Onboarding professional services (initial deployment + runbook + 1-week performance tuning): one-time $18,000 (estimate).
- We’ll include a one-page Mutual Action Plan and a DocuSign-ready quote.
